title: Sampling cliff and unlogged saturation playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: After the multi-tenant capacity incident on 2026-02-20 we discovered a correlated drop in sampled traces and missing saturation signals for tenant-facing API queues. This ticket captures the analysis of the sampling cliff (sudden reduction in trace sampling rate), the lack of per-tenant queue length metrics, and a playbook to prevent silent saturation in the Console ingestion pipeline.
impact_summary: Production incident: a burst in incoming requests caused queue growth but our dashboards did not surface per-tenant tail latency or queue saturation. Trace sampling dropped ~90% for the affected worker pool due to a misconfigured sampler bound to host-level CPU triggers. Result: customer-visible timeouts in Console routes, increased error budget burn for Dedicated customers, and delayed on-call detection.
notes_and_findings: Root cause: sampler threshold config inherited from old rollout (host-cpu-based) interacted badly with new autoscaler; during the spike sampler toggled off for the worker group.
Observation: no per-tenant queue-length metric existed for the Console ingestion path; only cluster-level queue size was shown which masked tenant-specific saturation.
Dashboard gap: alert thresholds were set on 95th latency but not on queue depth or sample rate; sampling rate dropped from ~12% to ~1% for the worst tenants.
Telemetry gap: trace spans from prefix-cache eviction paths were only sampled at debug level and rarely surfaced in production traces; coldstart path remained uninstrumented.
Mitigations during incident: manual sampler override, temporary throttling of low-priority background work, and scoped rollback of a knob that increased the sampler trigger sensitivity.
Follow-up risk: if autoscaler policies change again without coordinating sampler configs, similar blindspots could recur in other clusters.
Customer notes: 2 Dedicated customers reported intermittent timeouts; support tickets linked in postmortem.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant queue-length metric emitting for Console ingestion (sampled every 15s) visible in the Console dashboard and Prometheus scrapeable.
Sampler configuration decoupled from host-level CPU signals and maintained as a per-worker-group config with sane defaults and test coverage.
New saturation alert rule: fires when per-tenant queue growth > X for 3 consecutive windows OR sampling rate drops below 5% for 2 minutes.
Runbook updated with step-by-step playbook for investigating sampling cliffs and manual override procedure documented with exact CLI commands and RBAC roles.
One end-to-end test that simulates a synthetic burst validates sampler behavior, alert firing, and dashboard visibility in staging.
PR with implementation merged and deployed to a canary environment; engineering review completed and deployment plan scheduled for release-2026.03.

implementation_notes: Emit per-tenant queue_length as a histogram + gauge to support both dashboards and SLO-derived alerts; avoid cardinality explosion by rolling up to tenant_id prefix and sampling detailed tenant ids.
Sampler change must include feature flag off-by-default; a gradual rollout with canary for worker-group 'ingest-psi' is required.
Add integration test that injects synthetic traces and validates sampling rate metrics exposed via /metrics endpoint.
Coordinate with SRE to ensure Prometheus retention for high-cardinality sampling-rate metrics is acceptable; if not, use a separate high-cardinality metrics sink for short-lived retention.
Console UX owner will design a dashboard tile that shows queue depth, sample rate, tail latency, and a 'saturation score' for quick on-call triage.
Tag all related PRs with label 'ENG-47211' for tracking and release notes aggregation.
